extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIH R01 (PHS 398) grant applications, especially new investigators applying to NIAID/NIH
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated example of a completed PHS 398 / R01 application with NIAID reviewer annotations and form-specific instructions; intended to show how to prepare each required section (face page, abstract, biosketches, research plan, budget, human/animal protections) and what reviewers evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title length and descriptiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Title is descriptive, detailed, less than 56 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exceed 56-character length restrictions, including spaces. Title should be descriptive and concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face Page: required checkboxes and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete face page items (e.g., response to RFA/PA, PI name/degree/position/title, human subjects, vertebrate animals, new investigator), and include institutional identification and signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New investigators should check the 'Yes' box. Signatures of PI and institutional official must be in ink; 'Per' signatures are not acceptable. Institutional/administrative office typically completes some parts (e.g., official signing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract / Project Description content
rubrics_metrics.description: State the application's broad, long-term objectives and specific aims, making reference to the health relatedness of the project. Describe concisely the research design and methods for achieving these goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This abstract serves as a succinct, accurate description of the proposed work when separated from the application and will become public information if funded; do not include proprietary/confidential information. DO NOT EXCEED THE SPACE PROVIDED. Avoid summaries of past accomplishments and the use of the first person (per form instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — recommended structure and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with one-sentence description and significance; state long-term goal and its health significance; state hypothesis and specific reasons for hypothesis; describe specific aims and how each will be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the abstract a succinct summary that fits inside the space provided. Use active voice, strong action verbs; bolding and numbers can help guide the reader. (NIAID annotations promote clarity and active phrasing while the official form warns about first-person usage — balance form instructions and readability.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Key personnel listing format
rubrics_metrics.description: List key personnel starting with Principal Investigator; list all other key personnel in alphabetical order, last name first. Provide organization and role on project for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches information on resources and biosketch pages. Use continuation pages as needed to provide required information in the format shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI name printed on each page
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the principal investigator/program director must be provided at the top of each printed page and each continuation page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent header across all pages to avoid administrative issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch length & structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch may not exceed four pages. Items A (Positions and Honors) and B (Selected peer-reviewed publications) together may not exceed two of the four-page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified format: NAME, POSITION TITLE, EDUCATION/TRAINING table, A. Positions and Honors (chronological), B. Selected peer-reviewed publications (chronological), C. Research Support. Do not exceed page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch — Publications and research support rules
rubrics_metrics.description: List selected peer-reviewed publications in chronological order; do not include publications submitted or in preparation. Research Support: list selected ongoing or completed (during the last three years) federal and non-federal support, beginning with projects most relevant to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly indicate the overall goals of listed projects and your role (e.g., PI, Co-Investigator, Consultant). Do not list award amounts or percent effort in projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents / Research Plan organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Table of Contents with the required sections: Face Page; Description/Performance Sites/Personnel; Detailed Budget; Biographical Sketches; Resources; Research Plan (Specific Aims; Background and Significance; Preliminary Studies/Progress Report; Research Design and Methods), and other sections (Human Subjects, Vertebrate Animals, Literature Cited, Consortium arrangements, Letters of Support, Appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the order and include page numbers. Be aware of which items are limited in pages and which appendices are allowed or disallowed (see Appendix rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for Research Plan items A–D
rubrics_metrics.description: Items A–D (Specific Aims; Background and Significance; Preliminary Studies/Progress Report; Research Design and Methods) are not to exceed 25 pages total (SBIR/STTR Phase I differs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBIR/STTR Phase I: Items A–D limited to 15 pages. Observe program-specific page limits; plan material accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: clarity and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should state the hypothesis and list discrete aims; describe how each aim will be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear set of aims (three aims shown in sample) with rationale and achievable endpoints helps reviewers quickly understand the proposal's structure and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data / Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include preliminary results that support hypotheses and the feasibility of the proposed methods (e.g., cloning/purification, mutants, reporter constructs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-articulated preliminary results strengthen Approach and reduce perceived risk. Address any discrepancies or strain variability in preliminary data and discuss controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design and Methods (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe experimental design, methods, controls, and analyses to achieve aims; include well-controlled experiments and appropriate assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate reviewer concerns (e.g., background binding, strain variability) and include alternative strategies or pilot studies where appropriate. Correlate assays (e.g., Western blot, EMSA, reporter assays) with functional readouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects & inclusion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If human subjects are involved, complete required sections: Protection of Human Subjects, Inclusion of Women, Inclusion of Minorities, Inclusion of Children, and Data and Safety Monitoring Plan when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark appropriate boxes on face page. Data and Safety Monitoring Plan required if a Phase I–III clinical trial is proposed. Provide assurance numbers and documentation as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If vertebrate animals are used, indicate 'Yes' on face page and provide IACUC approval date and animal welfare assurance number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required approvals and justification; include species, numbers, and welfare considerations in the Vertebrate Animals section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget format and constraints (Modular budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide modular budget or detailed budget as required; indicate direct costs and total costs for initial and entire project period; keep within program limits (e.g., five-year maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be modest and justified. Percent effort for personnel must match the described work on project. For modular budgets, use the modular format and include a budget justification page. Note program-specific caps and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel effort consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage level of effort for each person must match work on project and must be reflected consistently across budget, budget justification, and biographical sketch/research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistencies between percent effort and described responsibilities raise administrative and scientific concerns; align all parts of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix and supporting materials rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix: Five collated sets; appendices are NOT PERMITTED for Phase I SBIR/STTR unless specifically solicited. Limit number of publications/manuscripts accepted for publication (not to exceed 10 in appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow appendix restrictions exactly; include only permitted materials and observe page/number limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear organization, schematics/figures where helpful, bolding and numbering to guide the reader; avoid clutter and unnecessary prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readable, well-organized proposals help reviewers understand complex interactions (e.g., regulatory loci) quickly. Use schematics to clarify mechanisms and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include proprietary/confidential information in public sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract and portions of the application may become public if funded, so do not include proprietary/confidential content in those sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sensitive information, if allowed, only in permissible parts or discuss with institutional officials. Favor descriptions that enable review without revealing trade secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH review criteria reflected in critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate Significance, Approach, Innovation, Investigators, Environment, and Overall Impact. Budget is also assessed for appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: does the project address an important problem? Approach: are methods rigorous, preliminary data adequate, and experiments well controlled? Innovation: does the project apply novel concepts or important new applications? Investigators: are PI and team qualified and productive? Environment: will institutional setting support success? Overall Impact: likelihood to exert strong influence on field. Address each explicitly in the application and tie aims, preliminary data, and personnel to these criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator qualifications and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Document PI and key personnel expertise, prior training, productivity (publication record), and specific roles/responsibilities on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight relevant skills and prior work that demonstrate ability to execute the proposed studies; collaborations and co-investigator expertise (e.g., techniques like SELEX) strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional environment, available equipment, reagents, strains, and collaborative arrangements that support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that necessary resources are already available or accessible; show how proximity and collaboration will facilitate the work and reduce risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing weaknesses and reviewer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate potential reviewer criticisms (e.g., unresolved roles of gene fragments, background binding issues, strain variability) and propose remedies (e.g., additional controls, pilot studies, constructing background mutants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss limitations and contingency plans in the Research Design and Methods or Introduction to Revised Application to reassure reviewers about feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: PI and institutional official must certify truthfulness and accept responsibility (face page assurances) and sign in ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification language warns about criminal/civil/administrative penalties for fraudulent claims. Ensure all required assurances are completed and signed properly.
